briefing.headline: Saturday is dry and sunny. Sunday's game looks mild, near 60°, but bring rain gear. Showers are possible during the game, and rain is more likely Sunday evening and night.

sections.title: Saturday
sections.text: **Sunny and dry.** It's cold early: upper 30s to mid 40s at 7 AM, so start with a jacket. By mid-afternoon it's in the low to mid 60s with light winds and lots of sun. The sun sets at 4:41 PM, and it's back into the 50s soon after, then the upper 40s by late evening.

sections.title: Sunday: game day
sections.text: **Cloudy and mild,** near 60° at the 1 PM kickoff with a light breeze. There's about a **40% chance of showers during the game**, more likely in the second half than at kickoff. If the rain comes, it's steadiest Sunday evening and overnight and could be heavy, an inch or more. There's also a real chance the whole day stays dry. No snow or thunder is expected.

sections.title: Monday morning
sections.text: Rain ends around daybreak. Then it turns **windy**, with gusts of 25 to 30 mph. Temperatures in the 50s start to fall in the afternoon.

sections.title: What to bring
sections.text: **Saturday:** a jacket or fleece for the early tailgate, long sleeves for the afternoon, and sunglasses, because the low November sun is bright. **Sunday:** long sleeves, a light jacket, and a **hooded rain jacket or poncho**, since umbrellas don't work in the stands. Wear shoes that can handle puddles. **Monday:** a wind-resistant jacket.

briefing.confidence: **Saturday: high.** **Sunday afternoon and night: low.** It depends on the path of a storm coming up the coast, and that should be clearer by Thursday. I'll update this briefing as it firms up.
briefing.fans:
High pressure near 1028 mb sits over the Mid-Atlantic on Saturday. A weak low forms off the Southeast coast and drifts north Sunday ahead of a Great Lakes cold front. GFS, AIFS and GEM bring its rain shield into Philadelphia Sunday afternoon into early Monday, with 0.6–1.8 in by Monday morning. The ECMWF IFS and ICON keep it offshore and dry. NBM splits the difference at about 0.4 in.

For the event, the ensembles give a 39–69% chance of 0.1 in or more and a 25–57% chance of 0.5 in or more. GEFS and ENS sit at the low end and AIFS ENS at the high end. The front crosses early Monday, and the wind turns northwest with gusts of 25–30 mph.
